newsitem.title: PERU: Ex-Ecuador leader aide says he persecuted.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Ecuador leader aide says he persecuted.

text.p: A former aide to deposed Ecuadorean President Abdala Bucaram on Monday told a Peruvian court studying his extradition that his life would be endangered if we were sent back to his country.

Enrique Villan, a former economic advisor to Bucaram, was arrested in March soon after he and his pregnant wife entered Peru illegally from Ecuador, where Congress declared Bucaram mentally unfit for the presidency and removed him from power.
The new government in Quito requested Villan's extradition and a special Peruvian court opend the hearings on Monday.
But Villan told jurors through his lawyer that his life would be jeopardised if he was sent back to Ecuador.

Villan "is being politically persecuted because of his job and because he was a founder of the Roldosista Party" of Bucaram, his attorney said. "Therefore his life and that of his family would be in danger."
A public hearing has been slated for Thursday.
